pointOfInterests.description: Possible hazard. This low water crossing is a hazard and should be portaged. I crossed it the somewhere around 600 cfs there are 3 or culverts under the road crossing, on the river left side. the river right side creates a  nasty hydralic (large boil line) as the water goes over the road. Be sure to portage if water is greater than 500 cfs.  Large tree down shortly after the crossing. Mandatory porage due to strainer after crossing. With in a couple hundred yards.

alerts.title: 2 Strainers 1 very bad hazard at high water greater than 500 cfs
alerts.detail:
If the water is high, greater than 500cfs, extreme strainer danger just walk past Chenaults Ln (Private Low-Water Crossing). The river turns left past the crossing and than immediately then back to the right with 100 or so yards past the crossing. After the river turns back to the right a large tree fell down on the River left bank blocking the flow of water and had caught multiple logs and debris. (Most Portage around)! See Chenaults Ln (Private Low-Water Crossing) hazard to see where on the map.

Also Past # mile Bridge another tree is down from River Left again Then one you can see ahead of time and Portage around easily on the left. At High flows this could be an issue however we had plenty of time to get exit the river and portage.

There is a low head dam after the 3 mile bridge there was a log on the the river right side. Portage is advisable or please scout before you attempt to run this drop.

detail.description:
Mostly a scenic float trip with multiple put-in/takeout options.  Numerous low-water crossings exist along the run, and [Texas Whitewater](http://philosophy.tamu.edu/%7Esdaniel/kayak.html) implies that at least most of these are runnable at high water, but all low-water crossings are potential hazards.  Exercise extreme caution around them.  Current beta is needed regarding the location of specific rapids along this stretch.

Distances and gradient measured using GIS tools in 2015.
